newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: BAK institute lowers 1996 Swiss growth forecast.
newsitem.headline: BAK institute lowers 1996 Swiss growth forecast.

text.p: Economic research institute BAK on Monday added to growing pessimism for Swiss economic prospects by lowering its forecast of 1996 growth for the second time in a month.

The institute, which is one of the country's top research bodies, said it expected gross domestic product (GDP) to shrink by 0.5 percent this year, revised from a forecast of a fall of 0.4 percent on August 20.
Swiss institutes and banks have dropped 1996 GDP projections for growth of around one percent at the start of the year, with recent estimates hovering at zero growth to a 0.5 percent fall.
BAK's forecast for 1997 real GDP growth was also lowered to 1.3 percent from 1.5 percent in its August report.
The institute singled out a continued decline in construction activity as well as reduced capital investment after strong spending for new equipment last year.
These factors helped push down second quarter GDP, reinforcing a broader pattern of weakness for the year caused in part by Swiss fanc strength against currencies of major export markets, BAK said.
"Switzerland has been in a period of stagnation since 1991," BAK said in a report, noting that average GDP change for the period 1990-1995 has been flat at zero percent.
